title: Altera, OQC, and NVIDIA Demonstrate Direct-RF FPGA Quantum System Controller Reference Design at SC26 - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Altera, OQC and NVIDIA showed at SC26 a quantum controller reference design that collapses superconducting-qubit control racks onto a single Agilex 9 Direct RF FPGA, with calibration and ML readout offloaded to NVIDIA GPUs over NVQLink; software GA is slated for January 2027.

insights.claim: Altera, Oxford Quantum Circuits (OQC) and NVIDIA demonstrated live at SC26 in Chicago an end-to-end quantum system controller reference design built on an Altera Agilex 9 Direct RF FPGA, linking FPGA control/readout electronics to an OQC superconducting processor and NVIDIA GPUs over NVQLink.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Altera is positioning its FPGA line as the control-plane silicon for quantum systems, a new niche end market alongside NVIDIA's hybrid quantum-GPU stack.
insights.locator: Altera Corporation, in collaboration with Oxford Quantum Circuits

insights.claim: Conventional superconducting quantum control stacks rely on multi-chassis racks of discrete DACs, analog mixers and local oscillators that scale poorly as qubit counts grow.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Control-electronics bulk and cost is a scaling bottleneck; vendors that collapse it onto single chips threaten discrete RF/test-instrument control-stack suppliers.
insights.locator: Conventional superconducting quantum control stacks require

insights.claim: The Agilex 9 Direct RF FPGA integrates direct-RF data converters and multi-channel frequency multiplexing on one programmable device, performing pulse synthesis, synchronized scheduling, qubit initialization and resonator spectroscopy without external analog conversion stages.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Watch for direct-RF FPGA/RFSoC integration as the path to denser, cheaper control per qubit; it competes with modular analog control racks.

insights.claim: In the Altera/OQC design, CUDA-driven GPU kernels over NVIDIA NVQLink offload compute-heavy calibration workflows and machine-learning readout classification from the real-time FPGA control loop.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Reinforces NVIDIA's strategy of making GPUs (and NVQLink/CUDA) the default classical co-processor in quantum systems regardless of qubit vendor.

insights.claim: NVQLink is accumulating third-party control-architecture integrations, including Quandela's photonic FPGA-to-GPU integration, CUDA-Q Logical ecosystem integrations, and CUDA-Q QEC 0.9.0 alongside Slurm 26.11 releases around SC26.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Breadth of NVQLink adoption across superconducting and photonic modalities suggests NVIDIA is becoming the hybrid quantum-classical interconnect standard.
insights.locator: Related QCR coverage of NVQLink control architectures

insights.claim: The Altera quantum controller software package includes a built-in controller emulation path letting developers validate firmware and hybrid algorithms before physical QPU deployment, with general release scheduled for January 2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: January 2027 GA is the milestone to watch for adoption of the reference design by QPU builders beyond OQC.
